clue.text: Stones set close in tin

definitions.meaning: sardine is an old word for a sard or carnelian, the 'sardine stone' of the Bible
the small fish famously packed tightly in a can

explanation.surface: Someone is setting gemstones snugly into a tin mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' looks like gems to be set; it is the first definition, from the biblical 'sardine stone'. 'Packed like sardines' gives the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is an archaic gem name, the reddish sard; the second describes small fish canned side by side.

clue.text: Tin-opener included in a whimsical etching

indicators.note: included in places the letter from Tin inside the other words

parts.note: quaint means oddly charming or whimsical

indicators.note: an opener is the beginning of a word, here the first letter of Tin

explanation.surface: A fanciful etching that shows a can opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin-opener' looks like a kitchen gadget; it means the first letter of Tin.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a printmaking method using acid on copper to give tones like watercolour, a kind of etched print.

clue.text: Store in which to go mad?

parts.note: to depart is to go away
mental is informal for mad

explanation.surface: A shop where people lose their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: A departmental store is an older name for a department store, so the word qualifies 'Store'.
explanation.definitionFit: An older phrase for a large shop selling goods in separate sections used this adjective before 'store'.

clue.text: Climax to bulletin in seven-year old language?

indicators.note: to here means added on, so the climax is attached to the end of the bulletin

parts.note: news is what a bulletin delivers
a peak is a high point or climax

explanation.surface: The dramatic end to a news bulletin was in the speech of a seven-year-old child.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven years before this puzzle was 1984, the year of Orwell's novel whose invented tongue is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four invents this pared-down official tongue; it was seven years old as a year at publication.

clue.text: Deputy of diminished reputation

indicators.note: diminished means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: standing means status or reputation

explanation.surface: A substitute whose good name has been tarnished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminished reputation' reads as disgrace; it means the word for reputation loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute who takes another's place temporarily acts as their deputy.

clue.text: Concert part shortened — supply the words for it

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert
pt is the short form of part

explanation.surface: Cut a section of the concert, then provide lyrics for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms in London.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre one feeds a forgetful actor the next line by whispering cues.

clue.text: Cheering Greyfriars' head boy

indicators.note: head means the first letter, here of Greyfriars'

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: The head boy at Greyfriars, Billy Bunter's school, is cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: Greyfriars is the boarding school of the Billy Bunter stories, so 'head boy' looks like a school post.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad tidings are heartening news, so the word can mean encouraging or joyful.

clue.text: Movement of earth makes one arrive by mistake

parts.note: to land is to arrive
a slip is a small error

explanation.surface: A landslide makes someone turn up accidentally.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of soil and rock sliding down a slope is a fall of ground.

clue.text: Fare from Mexico wrong — I get full amount back

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: back says the word for the full amount is read from right to left

parts.note: the full amount is all of it

explanation.surface: A complaint about Mexican food: it was wrong, and I want a full refund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word for full amount around; 'wrong' is a legal term here, a civil wrong rather than an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin flatbread of maize or wheat is a staple dish of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Unpleasant place in desert

definitions.meaning: a squalid, dreary spot, a hole

explanation.surface: A grim spot out in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotty location is called this in slang, and to leave a partner abruptly is the same word as a verb.

clue.text: Main debt ends at sea — far away, you could say

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The main debt is finally settled at sea, far off from land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the twelve letters of MAIN DEBT ENDS. 'Far away' means dreamy, lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forgetful and dreamy has their thoughts elsewhere, distant from the task in hand.

clue.text: Wild raver in passionate embrace can be frightening

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for passionate embrace

parts.note: necking is kissing and cuddling

indicators.note: wild means unruly and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild partygoer's passionate embrace can be scary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges the raver's letters to RVERA; the passionate embrace is old slang for kissing and cuddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that strains the nerves causes great anxiety or fear.

clue.text: Suggestion to every leader — tread carefully!

parts.note: a tip is a hint or suggestion

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of every

explanation.surface: Advice passed to each leader: step cautiously!
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on the balls of the feet is to move quietly and with care.

clue.text: Joined forces?

parts.note: read as police forces of many countries linked in one international body

explanation.surface: Did they team up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joined forces' reads as a phrase about allies; the forces are police services working together across borders.
explanation.definitionFit: The international criminal police organisation links national police services worldwide.

clue.text: Speeds daringly, out of gear

parts.note: gear means clothes, so this is someone dashing about naked

explanation.surface: A driver races recklessly with the car out of gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' suggests a car's gearbox; here it means clothing. Running naked through a crowd is the stunt described.
explanation.definitionFit: Running naked across a public place, such as a sports pitch, is the prank called this.

clue.text: Swift, for example — one in dire straits

indicators.note: in puts the letter for one inside the jumbled word
dire suggests a terrible, disordered state, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Jonathan Swift, a man in a dreadful plight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' rearranges STRAITS into SATRIST, and I goes inside it. 'Swift' is the satirist Jonathan Swift, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal, mocking society through ridicule.

clue.text: Whitewash accomplished in football competition

indicators.note: in places the word for accomplished inside the competition

parts.note: a cup is a knockout football competition such as the FA Cup
something over is done and finished

explanation.surface: A football tournament where the result was a crushing win, a whitewash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whitewash' suggests a heavy sporting defeat, which the surface plays on; here it means concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitewash is the hushing up of wrongdoing, a concealment of the facts.

clue.text: No point accommodating Omar's singer in a conservatory

parts.note: no is nothing, the round letter O

indicators.note: accommodating means holding, so the word for point houses the singer

parts.note: use is purpose, as in what's the point
Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat has 'and Thou beside me singing in the wilderness'

explanation.surface: It is pointless to put up a singer from Omar in a glasshouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thou' is the companion singing in FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam. The definition is by example: a conservatory is a building added on to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A subsidiary building attached to or near a main dwelling, such as a shed or glasshouse.

clue.text: Notable peacemakers set on general

indicators.note: set on means placed on top of, as this is a down clue

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
common means general or widespread

explanation.surface: Distinguished peacekeepers set upon a general.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare or out of the ordinary is remarkable, standing out from the rest.

clue.text: Joint wager — outside chance

indicators.note: outside says the word for wager goes around the word for chance

parts.note: a bet is a wager
risk is chance or hazard

explanation.surface: A shared bet on an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint wager' reads as a shared bet; 'Joint' is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cut of beef from the breast, a joint for roasting or braising.

clue.text: Artist using 'all of beauty's depth?

parts.note: beauty is only skin deep, and this artist works with needle and ink in the skin

explanation.surface: A painter who exploits every depth of beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'beauty is only skin deep' means beauty's whole depth is skin, the medium of this artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who marks designs into skin with inked needles is a body artist.

clue.text: Cross over the Atlantic?

parts.note: cross means bad-tempered, and the word sought is the American term for it

explanation.surface: Sailing across the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross over' looks like a voyage; it means irritable as said in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for cantankerous or grumpy, a dialect form of 'ordinary'.

clue.text: Dream of a happy medium?

parts.note: a medium here is a spiritualist, who may slip into a dreamlike state at a seance

explanation.surface: Wishing for a sensible compromise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy medium' means a compromise; read it as a contented spiritualist in a dreamlike state.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed, hypnotic state is like a dream, and spiritualists claim to enter one to reach the dead.

clue.text: Extremely rich supply of vehicles on the line

parts.note: rolling, as in rolling in it, means very wealthy
stock is a supply kept on hand

explanation.surface: A wealthy railway company has plenty of trains on its tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages, wagons and locomotives are collectively the trains that run on the track.

clue.text: Bassanio's choice of conduct

definitions.meaning: in The Merchant of Venice Bassanio wins Portia by picking the leaden casket

explanation.surface: Bassanio's choice of behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassanio picks the casket of the dull grey metal, and to guide or head something is the same word as a verb.

clue.text: One goes to a doctor, showing foot in two parts

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A patient visits a doctor to have a foot looked at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' suggests a body part sent to the doctor; in verse a foot is a metrical unit.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse, this metrical unit has two syllables, an unstressed followed by a stressed one.

clue.text: Fabulous swimmer may be yellow, you say, taking heroin?

parts.note: the Yellow Sea is a body of water off China, so one may say a sea is yellow
horse is a slang name for heroin

explanation.surface: A mythical swimmer might be a coward, people say, and on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' suggests cowardice; it names the Yellow Sea between China and Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth Neptune's chariot is drawn by these fishtailed steeds, and a real fish of the name also exists.

clue.text: On they go, all over the place, in the study of divine houses

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Off they travel everywhere, researching the homes of the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges ON THEY GO. The houses are dynasties of gods, not buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the account of the origin and lineage of the gods, their family trees as in Hesiod.
